subject: Post-demo: vendor differentiation checklist & validation plan
messages:

Subject: Post-demo: vendor differentiation checklist & validation plan

Hi Sarah / Evan —

Thanks for taking the time today — good discussion. Below is a concise recap of the pain points you called out, the success criteria you want to validate, and a prioritized list of probes we propose for the bakeoff. I attached an editable bakeoff matrix (redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx) so your team can add weights/criteria.

Key pain points you described
- P95 latency spikes during peak batch ingestion (esp. >100 concurrent sessions).
- Nonlinear token cost growth when calls use long context windows.
- Cache warming: inconsistent cold-to-warm transition behavior (KV cache hit variability).
- Operational complexity: rollouts/backfills require manual orchestration.

Primary goals for the evaluation
1) Consistent p95 < 400ms for 2k token streams at 95th percentile in our staging workload.
2) Predictable per-token unit economics that scale linearly with concurrency.
3) Reproducible cache behavior: cold/warm delta < 20% on tail latency.
4) Security/residency: VPC + customer-managed KMS required.

Context: you mentioned running a three-way test vs CloudAI and TorchServePro; we will keep comparisons explicit in the matrix.

Priority probes (proposed order) — objective, test, acceptance
1) Long-context latency sweep — 512 / 2k / 8k tokens; 50 / 200 concurrent sessions; accept if p95 < 400ms at 2k.
2) Cold vs warm start window — measure first 5 requests after cache flush vs steady-state; accept if cold/warm delta < 20%.
3) Throughput under tail load — synthetic spike to +60% of baseline for 15 minutes; must not exceed 5% error rate.
4) Model fallback behavior — simulate node loss and validate graceful fallback to smaller variants without >1s added latency.
5) Cost modeling pass — run typical month-to-month mix and produce per-token cost curve plus dedicated capacity quote.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Can you confirm the internal bakeoff stakeholders and preferred dates for a 2-week window (we suggested Jun 7–20)?
- Please add any additional weighting to the attached matrix so we align on scoring.
- Can Evan share sample trace logs or a small anonymized sample workload (S3 link) we can use to mirror your traffic pattern?

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (editable), priority-probes-checklist.md (short plan)

If this aligns, our Solutions team will prepare test harnesses and a Cloud/Private configuration matrix for the first wave.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Markus —

Thanks for the clear recap. This matches our notes. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Security/residency: we need evidence of KMS integrations and audit log retention for 12 months (SOC2 scope). Please include a short matrix of what you can provide in hosted vs private modes.
- For the long-context tests, please include a cert for sequence truncation / safety filters — we can't have unexpected token deletions.
- We will provide a 1GB anonymized trace from our staging bucket by May 28 (Evan will send the S3 link). That should be enough for your team to reproduce the skewed request lengths.

Scheduling: Jun 7–20 works for the team. Stakeholders: myself (product), Evan Brooks (CTO), plus two engineers — Laura Kim (backend) and Diego (infra). They will be observers on the initial run.

One ask on pricing: please include dedicated capacity pricing for a committed 95th-percentile throughput target and an overage metric. We need an apples-to-apples comparison with CloudAI's committed pool quote.

Thanks,
Sarah
Head of Product
NovaMed Systems
(signed)

Hi Sarah / team —

Quick technical notes and a proposed probe implementation. I put a short probe checklist in priority-probes-checklist.md (attached) and a small log schema in kv-cache-probe-log.txt that our harness will emit so you can map results back to your telemetry.

Implementation notes
- Long-context latency sweep: we'll run against a 3-node dedicated pool and a hosted run. For 8k tokens we'll test both full-precision and a quantized 4-bit variant to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Cache warming: we'll instrument KV-hits by model step; output will include per-request kv_hit boolean, prefetch time, and kv_lookup_us. The kv-cache-probe-log.txt has an example line.
- Failure/fallback: we'll orchestrate controlled node restarts at t+5m and validate the routing policy doesn't route to incompatible model variants.

Data/security
- KMS: hosted supports customer-managed KMS keys for workspace-level encryption. Private deployment supports HSM integrations (we'll list partners in the matrix).
- Audit logs: hosted can provide 12 months via the enterprise retention add-on (we'll include export examples).

Timeline & resources
- May 28: expect the S3 sample from NovaMed.
- Jun 2: Redwood will share the final test harness and an execution playbook for the Jun 7 start.
- Jun 7–11: Phase 1 runs (latency sweeps + kv probes).
- Jun 14–18: Phase 2 (throughput & failover tests + cost modeling).

Attachments (stubs): priority-probes-checklist.md — short list of commands and expected outputs; kv-cache-probe-log.txt — example log lines; redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx — criteria matrix.

If helpful I can paste a short example kv log here, otherwise we'll put sample output into the drive folder.
